```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

`multideconv` is an integrative pipeline for combining first- and second-generation cell type deconvolution methods from bulk RNA-seq data, as described in [Hurtado et al., 2025](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.04.29.651220v2.article-info).

## Installation

`multideconv` requires R >= 4.3.3. On R 4.3.0 to 4.3.2, first install a newer version of the `Matrix` package (R 4.3.3 already includes it):

```{r, eval=FALSE}
pak::pkg_install("Matrix@1.6-5")
```

To avoid GitHub API rate limit issues, set up a Personal Access Token (PAT) before installing:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# install.packages(c("usethis", "gitcreds"))
usethis::create_github_token()
gitcreds::gitcreds_set()
```

Install `multideconv` from GitHub:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("VeraPancaldiLab/multideconv")
```

Two of the default methods of `compute.deconvolution()`, DeconRNASeq and DWLS, are optional dependencies and are not installed automatically. Install them with:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
pak::pkg_install(c("bioc/DeconRNASeq", "omnideconv/DWLS"))
```

DeconRNASeq was removed from Bioconductor (release 3.22), so it is installed from Bioconductor's GitHub mirror.

## Tutorials

Step-by-step tutorials are available in the **Articles** section of the navigation bar:

- **Deconvolution with default methods** — run first-generation deconvolution and access built-in signatures
- **Cell type subgroup analysis** — derive cell-type subgroups and build a deconvolution dictionary
- **Single-cell deconvolution** — construct metacells and apply second-generation methods
- **Pseudo-bulk profiles and benchmarking** — create pseudo-bulk data, generate custom signatures, and benchmark performance
- **Machine learning workflows** — use subgroup features in cross-validated ML models

## Citation

If you use `multideconv` in a scientific publication, please cite:

> Hurtado, M., Essabbar, A., Khajavi, L., & Pancaldi, V. (2025). *multideconv – Integrative pipeline for cell type deconvolution from bulk RNAseq using first and second generation methods.* bioRxiv. <https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.04.29.651220>

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	
5	## What This Package Does
6	
7	**multideconv** is an R package providing an integrative pipeline for combining multiple cell type deconvolution methods (both first- and second-generation) from bulk RNA-seq data. It harmonizes outputs across methods, removes redundant cell types via correlation analysis, and identifies robust cell subgroups.
8	
9	## Working Rules
10	
11	- **Describe a fix and get approval before editing code.** Report the bug, the proposed change and how it was verified; apply only after the user agrees.
12	- **Test with small data only.** The dev machine has ~15 GB RAM. Subsample (e.g. ~200 cells x 2,000 genes, 4 bulk samples), use 1 worker/core, cap runs with `timeout`, and run heavy methods one at a time. Never compile large packages (e.g. Seurat) from source with many cores; use Posit Package Manager binaries into a temporary library instead.
13	- Never write test output into the package tree or the user's home; run in a temp directory (`withr::local_tempdir()`) and clean up.
14	
15	## Development Commands
16	
17	```r
18	devtools::load_all()     # interactive development
19	devtools::document()     # regenerate man/ + NAMESPACE (required after any roxygen change)
20	devtools::test()         # testthat suite in tests/testthat/
21	devtools::check()        # R CMD check
22	pkgdown::check_pkgdown() # verify _pkgdown.yml before pushing
23	shiny::runApp('inst/shiny', host='127.0.0.1', port=3838)
24	```
25	
26	### CI (GitHub Actions)
27	
28	- `R-CMD-check.yaml` fails on any **WARNING**. A roxygen block without a regenerated `.Rd` (forgetting `devtools::document()`) produces "Undocumented code objects" and fails CI.
29	- `pkgdown.yaml` fails if any documented topic is missing from the `reference:` index in `_pkgdown.yml`. Every new exported/documented function must be added there (sections: Main, Benchmarking, Single cell functions, Helpers = exported helpers, Internal = not exported, Package Data) or marked `@keywords internal`.
30	- Exported functions (12): `compute.deconvolution`, `compute.deconvolution.analysis`, `aggregate_cell_groups`, `replicate_deconvolution_subgroups`, `compute.benchmark`, `compute.subgroup.pathways`, `prepare_multideconv_folds`, `create_metacells`, `create_sc_pseudobulk`, `create_sc_signatures`, `get_cell_type_nomenclature`, `standardize_celltype_colnames`. Every other function is tagged `@keywords internal` (`.onLoad` uses `@noRd`); new internal functions must be too. Every `@param` must be documented, otherwise R CMD check warns (`devtools::check_man()` catches it quickly).
31	- Non-package files at top level must be listed in `.Rbuildignore` (CLAUDE.md, Results, Rplots.pdf, launch_app.R, .vscode, .claude, pypath_log, omnipathr-log, ...). Do not ignore `vignettes/Results/`: the a4 vignette embeds `vignettes/Results/Benchmark.png`.
32	
33	## Installation
34	
35	```r
36	pak::pkg_install("VeraPancaldiLab/multideconv")
37	```
38	
39	Several dependencies come from GitHub remotes (omnideconv, immunedeconv, DWLS, BayesPrism, MOMF, `BisqueRNA=cozygene/bisque`, `bioc/DeconRNASeq`) — see `DESCRIPTION`. A remote whose repo name differs from the package name needs the `Package=` prefix, otherwise pak cannot match it.
40	
41	**Effective minimum R is 4.3.3** (it ships Matrix 1.6-5; current `SeuratObject` needs Matrix >= 1.6-4, and current Matrix needs R >= 4.4). DESCRIPTION keeps `R (>= 4.3)` on purpose: `R (>= 4.3.3)` gives the `--as-cran` WARNING "Dependence on R version not with patchlevel 0", which fails CI. The README/vignette tell R 4.3.0–4.3.2 users to run `pak::pkg_install("Matrix@1.6-5")` first (verified to resolve on R 4.3.1). `Deriv` (reached via `ggpubr → rstatix → car → pbkrtest → doBy`, which omnideconv still pulls in) needs R >= 4.5 in its current version, so it is pinned to 4.2.0 through `Remotes: Deriv=url::...` and listed in Imports, because pak only applies a `Remotes` pin to a direct dependency (unused import → harmless R CMD check NOTE). DeconRNASeq was removed from Bioconductor 3.22, hence the `bioc/DeconRNASeq` GitHub mirror; it and DWLS are Suggests although they are default methods. `ggpubr` and `glmGamPoi` were replaced in code (`ggtext::element_markdown(angle = 45, ...)`; per-sample sums via a sparse cells x samples indicator product in `create_sc_pseudobulk()`); do not reintroduce them. `hdWGCNA` is an optional runtime dependency (`pak::pkg_install("smorabit/hdWGCNA")`) needed only by `create_metacells()`; it is not a `Remote` and is checked via `requireNamespace()`. `Seurat` is in Suggests: functions using it (`create_metacells()`, `create_sc_pseudobulk()`) must check `requireNamespace("Seurat")` first.
42	
43	CIBERSORTx requires credentials and Docker (image `cibersortx/fractions`). AutogeneS runs in omnideconv's Python conda env `r-omnideconv` (module `autogenes`).
44	
45	## Architecture
46	
47	All functions live in a single file: `R/cell_deconvolution.R` (~3,000 lines). This is intentional.
48	
49	### Core Pipeline Flow
50	
51	1. **`compute.deconvolution()`** — TPM-normalizes (`normalized = TRUE` means "normalize the input"), runs Quantiseq plus the signature-based methods over every signature (bundled + `Results/custom_signatures/`), then standardizes names via `compute.deconvolution.preprocessing()`. Per-method/signature results are cached as `Results/deconv_<method>_<sig>_<data id>.rds` while running (crash recovery; the data id is a short md5 of the TPM matrix, so a cache is only reused for the same input) and deleted at the end. Signature names are the file name without `.txt` (`tools::file_path_sans_ext()`) everywhere; `Results/` is removed again if it was created only for the cache. It stops with a clear error if no method produced output.
52	   - **CBSX without credentials is skipped with a warning** (it is in the default `methods`), not a hard error.
53	   - `doParallel = TRUE` with `workers = NULL` uses `detectCores() - 1`.
54	2. **`compute.deconvolution.analysis()`** — removes zero-heavy features (`zero_thr`) and features that barely vary (`cv_thr`: coefficient of variation sd/mean below 0.1, each feature judged on its own so rare cell types are not penalised), splits by cell type (`compute.cell.types()`), then groups the features of each cell type by complete-linkage hierarchical clustering of their correlations (`compute_subgroups()`, correlations from `corr_subgroups()`): features form a subgroup only if every pair correlates >= `corr` (non-significant correlations, p >= 0.05, count as 0), and each subgroup is summarised by the row median of its members. Features are sorted by name before clustering, so ties are broken the same way and the result does not depend on column order. There is no pruning step and no `seed` (`removeCorrelatedFeatures()`, `prune_thr` and `seed` were removed). With `batch`, correlations are partial correlations (`ppcor`) controlling for batch.
55	3. **`replicate_deconvolution_subgroups()`** — applies the learned subgroups (median of the member features) to a new cohort, one subgroup at a time in composition order, so compositions whose members are earlier subgroups (results saved with older versions) still work. On the training data it reproduces the "Deconvolution matrix" exactly.
56	4. **`prepare_multideconv_folds()`** — fold-aware feature construction for pipeML (see below).
57	5. **Single-cell workflow** — `create_metacells()` → `create_sc_pseudobulk()` / `create_sc_signatures()` → `compute.deconvolution(sc_deconv = TRUE, ...)`, which calls the internal `compute_sc_deconvolution_methods()`.
58	
59	### Method Categories
60	
61	- **First-generation / signature-based**: Quantiseq (`immunedeconv`, TIL10), EpiDISH, DeconRNASeq, DWLS, CIBERSORTx (CBSX, via `omnideconv`), MOMF (needs `sc_matrix`). MCP-counter and xCell were removed (helpers kept commented out).
62	- **Second-generation** (internal `compute_sc_deconvolution_methods()`, run via `compute.deconvolution(sc_deconv = TRUE)`, through `omnideconv`, need a single-cell reference): AutogeneS, BayesPrism, Bisque, CPM, MuSiC, SCDC. AutogeneS and CPM are slow even on tiny inputs (tens of minutes / >5 min).
63	
64	### Method-specific pitfalls
65	
66	- **Result element names differ per method** and are extracted by name (`$proportions`, `$theta`, `$bulk.props`, `$cellTypePredictions`, `$Est.prop.weighted`, `$prop.est.mvw`, `$cell.prop`). A wrong name silently yields `NULL` and the method disappears from the output. BisqueRNA returns `bulk.props` as **cell types x samples**, so it is transposed; every method must end up samples x cell types.
67	- **CIBERSORTx fallback** (`computeCBSX()`, also used by the parallel version): omnideconv defaults `input_dir`/`output_dir` to `tempdir()`. On some machines the container crashes (error code 139, `..._Results.txt does not exist`). Only on that error it retries once with `~/user_projects/cibersort/{input,output}` (created on demand); any other error is re-raised.
68	- `name_object` / `name_signature` default to `"scRNAseq"` / `"custom"` when `NULL`, to avoid `Method__cell` names and `DWLS--scRNAseq.txt` files.
69	
70	### Metacells (Seurat 4 and 5)
71	
72	`create_metacells()` / `process_group()` must work with both Seurat 4 (SeuratObject 4.x, `Assay`) and Seurat 5 (SeuratObject 5.x, `Assay5`, possibly split layers). Verified on Seurat 4.4.0 and 5.5.1.
73	- Read counts from the metacell object's own assay (`DefaultAssay(meta)`; hdWGCNA keeps the input's default assay, e.g. `SCT`), with `LayerData(layer = "counts")` on SeuratObject >= 5 and `GetAssayData(slot = "counts")` on 4. The `slot` argument is defunct in recent SeuratObject 5 and `layer` does not exist in 4.
74	- Group subsets are built by selecting cell names from the metadata with `which()` and calling `subset(data, cells = cells_use)`. Do **not** use `subset(subset = samples_ids == patient, ...)`: a metadata column named e.g. `patient` shadows the loop variable and silently returns empty groups. `which()` handles `NA` labels.
75	- `subset()` is base R's S3 generic; it dispatches to `SeuratObject`'s `subset.Seurat`. `Seurat::subset` does not exist — do not write it.
76	- The user's `future` plan is saved and restored (`on.exit`), also on error. hdWGCNA's `MetacellsByGroups()` needs a `pca` reduction already present in the input object.
77	- Metacells are built with `MetacellsByGroups(mode = "sum")` (integer summed counts) and default `k = 15`, `max_shared = 10`. `max_shared` must stay below `k`: with `max_shared = k` metacells can overlap completely and you get about one metacell per cell.
78	
79	### Cross-validation folds (`prepare_multideconv_folds()` ↔ pipeML)
80	
81	- `folds` is a list of **training** row indices (e.g. `caret::createMultiFolds`); the test set is the complement.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What This Package Does

**multideconv** is an R package providing an integrative pipeline for combining multiple cell type deconvolution methods (both first- and second-generation) from bulk RNA-seq data. It harmonizes outputs across methods, removes redundant cell types via correlation analysis, and identifies robust cell subgroups.

## Working Rules

- **Describe a fix and get approval before editing code.** Report the bug, the proposed change and how it was verified; apply only after the user agrees.
- **Test with small data only.** The dev machine has ~15 GB RAM. Subsample (e.g. ~200 cells x 2,000 genes, 4 bulk samples), use 1 worker/core, cap runs with `timeout`, and run heavy methods one at a time. Never compile large packages (e.g. Seurat) from source with many cores; use Posit Package Manager binaries into a temporary library instead.
- Never write test output into the package tree or the user's home; run in a temp directory (`withr::local_tempdir()`) and clean up.

## Development Commands

```r
devtools::load_all()     # interactive development
devtools::document()     # regenerate man/ + NAMESPACE (required after any roxygen change)
devtools::test()         # testthat suite in tests/testthat/
devtools::check()        # R CMD check
pkgdown::check_pkgdown() # verify _pkgdown.yml before pushing
shiny::runApp('inst/shiny', host='127.0.0.1', port=3838)
```

### CI (GitHub Actions)

- `R-CMD-check.yaml` fails on any **WARNING**. A roxygen block without a regenerated `.Rd` (forgetting `devtools::document()`) produces "Undocumented code objects" and fails CI.
- `pkgdown.yaml` fails if any documented topic is missing from the `reference:` index in `_pkgdown.yml`. Every new exported/documented function must be added there (sections: Main, Benchmarking, Single cell functions, Helpers = exported helpers, Internal = not exported, Package Data) or marked `@keywords internal`.
- Exported functions (12): `compute.deconvolution`, `compute.deconvolution.analysis`, `aggregate_cell_groups`, `replicate_deconvolution_subgroups`, `compute.benchmark`, `compute.subgroup.pathways`, `prepare_multideconv_folds`, `create_metacells`, `create_sc_pseudobulk`, `create_sc_signatures`, `get_cell_type_nomenclature`, `standardize_celltype_colnames`. Every other function is tagged `@keywords internal` (`.onLoad` uses `@noRd`); new internal functions must be too. Every `@param` must be documented, otherwise R CMD check warns (`devtools::check_man()` catches it quickly).
- Non-package files at top level must be listed in `.Rbuildignore` (CLAUDE.md, Results, Rplots.pdf, launch_app.R, .vscode, .claude, pypath_log, omnipathr-log, ...). Do not ignore `vignettes/Results/`: the a4 vignette embeds `vignettes/Results/Benchmark.png`.

## Installation

```r
pak::pkg_install("VeraPancaldiLab/multideconv")
```

Several dependencies come from GitHub remotes (omnideconv, immunedeconv, DWLS, BayesPrism, MOMF, `BisqueRNA=cozygene/bisque`, `bioc/DeconRNASeq`) — see `DESCRIPTION`. A remote whose repo name differs from the package name needs the `Package=` prefix, otherwise pak cannot match it.

**Effective minimum R is 4.3.3** (it ships Matrix 1.6-5; current `SeuratObject` needs Matrix >= 1.6-4, and current Matrix needs R >= 4.4). DESCRIPTION keeps `R (>= 4.3)` on purpose: `R (>= 4.3.3)` gives the `--as-cran` WARNING "Dependence on R version not with patchlevel 0", which fails CI. The README/vignette tell R 4.3.0–4.3.2 users to run `pak::pkg_install("Matrix@1.6-5")` first (verified to resolve on R 4.3.1). `Deriv` (reached via `ggpubr → rstatix → car → pbkrtest → doBy`, which omnideconv still pulls in) needs R >= 4.5 in its current version, so it is pinned to 4.2.0 through `Remotes: Deriv=url::...` and listed in Imports, because pak only applies a `Remotes` pin to a direct dependency (unused import → harmless R CMD check NOTE). DeconRNASeq was removed from Bioconductor 3.22, hence the `bioc/DeconRNASeq` GitHub mirror; it and DWLS are Suggests although they are default methods. `ggpubr` and `glmGamPoi` were replaced in code (`ggtext::element_markdown(angle = 45, ...)`; per-sample sums via a sparse cells x samples indicator product in `create_sc_pseudobulk()`); do not reintroduce them. `hdWGCNA` is an optional runtime dependency (`pak::pkg_install("smorabit/hdWGCNA")`) needed only by `create_metacells()`; it is not a `Remote` and is checked via `requireNamespace()`. `Seurat` is in Suggests: functions using it (`create_metacells()`, `create_sc_pseudobulk()`) must check `requireNamespace("Seurat")` first.

CIBERSORTx requires credentials and Docker (image `cibersortx/fractions`). AutogeneS runs in omnideconv's Python conda env `r-omnideconv` (module `autogenes`).

## Architecture

All functions live in a single file: `R/cell_deconvolution.R` (~3,000 lines). This is intentional.

### Core Pipeline Flow

1. **`compute.deconvolution()`** — TPM-normalizes (`normalized = TRUE` means "normalize the input"), runs Quantiseq plus the signature-based methods over every signature (bundled + `Results/custom_signatures/`), then standardizes names via `compute.deconvolution.preprocessing()`. Per-method/signature results are cached as `Results/deconv_<method>_<sig>_<data id>.rds` while running (crash recovery; the data id is a short md5 of the TPM matrix, so a cache is only reused for the same input) and deleted at the end. Signature names are the file name without `.txt` (`tools::file_path_sans_ext()`) everywhere; `Results/` is removed again if it was created only for the cache. It stops with a clear error if no method produced output.
   - **CBSX without credentials is skipped with a warning** (it is in the default `methods`), not a hard error.
   - `doParallel = TRUE` with `workers = NULL` uses `detectCores() - 1`.
2. **`compute.deconvolution.analysis()`** — removes zero-heavy features (`zero_thr`) and features that barely vary (`cv_thr`: coefficient of variation sd/mean below 0.1, each feature judged on its own so rare cell types are not penalised), splits by cell type (`compute.cell.types()`), then groups the features of each cell type by complete-linkage hierarchical clustering of their correlations (`compute_subgroups()`, correlations from `corr_subgroups()`): features form a subgroup only if every pair correlates >= `corr` (non-significant correlations, p >= 0.05, count as 0), and each subgroup is summarised by the row median of its members. Features are sorted by name before clustering, so ties are broken the same way and the result does not depend on column order. There is no pruning step and no `seed` (`removeCorrelatedFeatures()`, `prune_thr` and `seed` were removed). With `batch`, correlations are partial correlations (`ppcor`) controlling for batch.
3. **`replicate_deconvolution_subgroups()`** — applies the learned subgroups (median of the member features) to a new cohort, one subgroup at a time in composition order, so compositions whose members are earlier subgroups (results saved with older versions) still work. On the training data it reproduces the "Deconvolution matrix" exactly.
4. **`prepare_multideconv_folds()`** — fold-aware feature construction for pipeML (see below).
5. **Single-cell workflow** — `create_metacells()` → `create_sc_pseudobulk()` / `create_sc_signatures()` → `compute.deconvolution(sc_deconv = TRUE, ...)`, which calls the internal `compute_sc_deconvolution_methods()`.

- **First-generation / signature-based**: Quantiseq (`immunedeconv`, TIL10), EpiDISH, DeconRNASeq, DWLS, CIBERSORTx (CBSX, via `omnideconv`), MOMF (needs `sc_matrix`). MCP-counter and xCell were removed (helpers kept commented out).

- **Result element names differ per method** and are extracted by name (`$proportions`, `$theta`, `$bulk.props`, `$cellTypePredictions`, `$Est.prop.weighted`, `$prop.est.mvw`, `$cell.prop`). - **CIBERSORTx fallback** (`computeCBSX()`, also used by the parallel version): omnideconv defaults `input_dir`/`output_dir` to `tempdir()`. On some machines the container crashes (error code 139, `..._Results.txt does not exist`). Only on that error it retries once with `~/user_projects/cibersort/{input,output}` (created on demand); any other error is re-raised.
- `name_object` / `name_signature` default to `"scRNAseq"` / `"custom"` when `NULL`, to avoid `Method__cell` names and `DWLS--scRNAseq.txt` files.

### Metacells (Seurat 4 and 5)

`create_metacells()` / `process_group()` must work with both Seurat 4 (SeuratObject 4.x, `Assay`) and Seurat 5 (SeuratObject 5.x, `Assay5`, possibly split layers). Verified on Seurat 4.4.0 and 5.5.1.

The `slot` argument is defunct in recent SeuratObject 5 and `layer` does not exist in 4.
- Group subsets are built by selecting cell names from the metadata with `which()` and calling `subset(data, cells = cells_use)`. Do **not** use `subset(subset = samples_ids == patient, ...)`: a metadata column named e.g. `patient` shadows the loop variable and silently returns empty groups. `which()` handles `NA` labels.
- `subset()` is base R's S3 generic; it dispatches to `SeuratObject`'s `subset.Seurat`. `Seurat::subset` does not exist — do not write it.
- The user's `future` plan is saved and restored (`on.exit`), also on error. hdWGCNA's `MetacellsByGroups()` needs a `pca` reduction already present in the input object.
- Metacells are built with `MetacellsByGroups(mode = "sum")` (integer summed counts) and default `k = 15`, `max_shared = 10`. `max_shared` must stay below `k`: with `max_shared = k` metacells can overlap completely and you get about one metacell per cell.

---
title: "Deconvolution with default methods"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Deconvolution with default methods}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

```{r setup}
library(multideconv)
```

## **Deconvolution with default methods**

The basic function is to perform cell type deconvolution using six default methods (`quanTIseq`, `DeconRNASeq`, `CIBERSORTx`, `EpiDISH`, `DWLS`, `MOMF`) and nine default signatures (see paper [Hurtado et al., 2025](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.04.29.651220v2.article-info)). The function accepts either raw counts or TPM-normalized counts as input (with genes as SYMBOL).

**NOTE:** If you plan to use `CIBERSORTx`, you must provide your credentials (see README for details). The resulting deconvolution matrix is automatically saved in the `Results/` directory.

The output includes all combinations of deconvolution features, method-signature-cell type.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
bulk = multideconv::raw_counts
deconv = compute.deconvolution(raw.counts = bulk, 
                               methods = c("Quantiseq", "Epidish", 
                                           "DeconRNASeq", "DWLS","MOMF"), 
                               normalized = TRUE, 
                               return = TRUE, 
                               file_name = "Tutorial")
```

To run only specific signatures, use the `signatures_select` argument. If `NULL` (default), all available signatures (package + custom from `Results/custom_signatures/`) are used:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
deconv = compute.deconvolution(raw.counts = bulk,
                               methods = c("Quantiseq", "DeconRNASeq"),
                               normalized = TRUE,
                               signatures_select = c("BPRNACan", "LM22"),
                               return = TRUE,
                               file_name = "Tutorial")
```

To speed up computation, `multideconv` supports parallelization. Set `doParallel = TRUE` and specify the number of workers based on your system's resources:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
deconv = compute.deconvolution(raw.counts = bulk, 
                               methods = "DWLS", 
                               normalized = TRUE, 
                               return = TRUE, 
                               file_name = "Tutorial", 
                               doParallel = TRUE, 
                               workers = 3)
```

Once deconvolution is complete, pass the result to `compute.deconvolution.analysis()` to reduce redundancy, group correlated features into subgroups, and (optionally) correct for batch/cohort effects — see the [Cell type subgroup analysis](a4_subgroups.html) article for a full walkthrough including the `batch` parameter and pathway characterisation with `compute.subgroup.pathways()`.

## **Cell type signatures**

In order to access the default signatures `multideconv` provides, you can do the following:

To list all signatures

```{r}
path <- system.file("signatures/", package = "multideconv")
list.files(path)
```

To access a specific signature

```{r}
signature = read.delim(paste0(path, "CBSX-Melanoma-scRNAseq.txt"))
head(signature)
```

Set `normalized = FALSE` when passing already-TPM-normalized data. Input must be linear TPM, not log-transformed — log2TPM data must first be reversed (e.g. `2^x - 1` if produced with `log2(TPM+1)`).

- `get_cell_type_nomenclature()` is the canonical vocabulary (43 names incl. `uncharacterized_cell`) — the single source of truth for classifying cell types (e.g. into immune vs. stromal groups) in any downstream script.
- Both `compute.deconvolution()` and `compute.deconvolution.analysis()` hardcode writing to a relative `Results/` directory — to control output location, `setwd()` into the desired output folder first, then flatten/move the generated `Results/` subfolder as needed.

tpm <- (2^as.matrix(log2tpm)) - 1

  verbose = TRUE,
  file_name = "Gide"
)

  "B.cells", "B.naive.cells", "B.memory.cells", "Macrophages.cells", "Macrophages.M0",
  "Macrophages.M1", "Macrophages.M2", "Monocytes", "Neutrophils", "NK.cells",

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
# TME (immune/stromal) characterization of the Gide melanoma ICB cohort using multideconv.

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(multideconv)
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(pheatmap)
  library(RColorBrewer)
})

set.seed(1)

work_dir <- "/home/marcelo.hurtado/Documents/tme_analysis/85d224db4e/work"
data_dir <- file.path(work_dir, "data")
results_dir <- file.path(work_dir, "results")

## ---- 1. Load data ----------------------------------------------------------

log2tpm <- read.delim(file.path(data_dir, "Gide_log2TPM.txt"), check.names = FALSE, row.names = 1)
coldata <- read.table(file.path(data_dir, "colData_all.txt"), header = TRUE, sep = " ", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

gide_clin <- coldata[coldata$Cohort == "Gide", ]
stopifnot(setequal(colnames(log2tpm), gide_clin$Sample_id))
gide_clin <- gide_clin[match(colnames(log2tpm), gide_clin$Sample_id), ]
rownames(gide_clin) <- gide_clin$Sample_id

## Reverse log2(TPM + 1) back to linear TPM scale (multideconv expects raw counts or linear TPM)
tpm <- (2^as.matrix(log2tpm)) - 1
tpm[tpm < 0] <- 0

## ---- 2. Run deconvolution (first-generation methods, no scRNA-seq reference available) ----

old_wd <- getwd()
setwd(results_dir)

deconv <- compute.deconvolution(
  raw.counts = tpm,
  methods = c("Quantiseq", "Epidish", "DeconRNASeq", "DWLS"),
  normalized = FALSE,
  doParallel = TRUE,
  workers = 4,
  return = TRUE,
  file_name = "Gide"
)

## ---- 3. Reduce redundancy / build per-cell-type subgroups ------------------

analysis <- compute.deconvolution.analysis(
  deconv,
  corr = 0.7,
  corr_type = "spearman",
  return = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  file_name = "Gide"
)

## Flatten the package's hardcoded Results/ subfolder into results/
if (dir.exists("Results")) {
  for (f in list.files("Results", full.names = TRUE)) {
    file.rename(f, file.path(results_dir, basename(f)))
  }
  unlink("Results", recursive = TRUE)
}

setwd(old_wd)

subgroup_mat <- analysis[["Deconvolution matrix"]]

## ---- 4. Classify cell types into Immune / Stromal / Other ------------------

immune_cells <- c(
  "B.cells", "B.naive.cells", "B.memory.cells", "Macrophages.cells", "Macrophages.M0",
  "Macrophages.M1", "Macrophages.M2", "Monocytes", "Neutrophils", "NK.cells",
  "NK.activated", "NK.resting", "NKT.cells", "CD4.cells", "CD4.memory.activated",
  "CD4.memory.resting", "CD4.naive", "CD8.cells", "CD4.regulatory", "CD4.non.regulatory",
  "T.cells.helper", "T.cells.gamma.delta", "Dendritic.cells", "Dendritic.activated.cells",
  "Dendritic.resting.cells", "Eosinophils", "Plasma", "Mast.cells", "Mast.activated.cells",
  "Mast.resting.cells", "Dendritic.plasmacytoid.cells", "Myeloid.cells", "Basophils",
  "T.cells.proliferative"
)
stromal_cells <- c("Endothelial", "Myocytes", "Fibroblasts", "CAF", "Pericytes", "Mural.cells")
other_cells <- c("Cancer", "Epithelial")

celltype_of_subgroup <- sub("_Subgroup\\.[0-9]+$", "", colnames(subgroup_mat))
category <- case_when(
  celltype_of_subgroup %in% immune_cells ~ "Immune",
  celltype_of_subgroup %in% stromal_cells ~ "Stromal",
  celltype_of_subgroup %in% other_cells ~ "Other",
  TRUE ~ "Unassigned"
)

feature_annot <- data.frame(
  Subgroup = colnames(subgroup_mat),
  Cell_type = celltype_of_subgroup,
  Category = category,
  row.names = colnames(subgroup_mat),
  check.names = FALSE
)
write.csv(feature_annot, file.path(results_dir, "Feature_cell_type_annotation_Gide.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## ---- 5. Composite Immune / Stromal scores per sample ------------------------
## Two-level z-scoring: subgroups of the same cell type are first averaged (so a
## cell type estimated by many correlated method-signature combinations does not
## dominate), then cell types are averaged uniformly within each category.

z_subgroups <- scale(as.matrix(subgroup_mat))

celltype_z <- sapply(split(colnames(subgroup_mat), celltype_of_subgroup), function(cols) {
  rowMeans(z_subgroups[, cols, drop = FALSE])
})
rownames(celltype_z) <- rownames(subgroup_mat)

celltype_category <- case_when(
  colnames(celltype_z) %in% immune_cells ~ "Immune",
  colnames(celltype_z) %in% stromal_cells ~ "Stromal",
  colnames(celltype_z) %in% other_cells ~ "Other",
  TRUE ~ "Unassigned"
)

scores <- data.frame(
  Sample_id = rownames(celltype_z),
  Immune_Score = rowMeans(celltype_z[, celltype_category == "Immune", drop = FALSE]),
  Stromal_Score = rowMeans(celltype_z[, celltype_category == "Stromal", drop = FALSE]),
  Other_Score = rowMeans(celltype_z[, celltype_category == "Other", drop = FALSE]),
  check.names = FALSE
)
scores$Immune_minus_Stromal <- scores$Immune_Score - scores$Stromal_Score

scores <- merge(scores, gide_clin[, c("Sample_id", "Response", "Therapy")], by = "Sample_id")
scores <- scores[, c("Sample_id", "Immune_Score", "Stromal_Score", "Other_Score", "Immune_minus_Stromal", "Response", "Therapy")]

scores <- scores[order(-scores$Immune_Score), ]
scores$Immune_Rank <- seq_len(nrow(scores))

write.csv(scores, file.path(results_dir, "Immune_Stromal_scores_Gide.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## ---- 6. Plots ---------------------------------------------------------------

## 6a. Ranked barplot of Immune Score per patient, colored by Response
plot_df <- scores
plot_df$Sample_id <- factor(plot_df$Sample_id, levels = plot_df$Sample_id[order(plot_df$Immune_Score)])

p_rank <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Sample_id, y = Immune_Score, fill = Response)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(R = "#1b9e77", NR = "#d95f02")) +
  labs(title = "Gide cohort - immune infiltration ranking", x = NULL,
       y = "Immune Score (mean z-score across immune cell types)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 8) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 5))

ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "Immune_score_ranking_Gide.pdf"), p_rank, width = 7, height = 14)
ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "Immune_score_ranking_Gide.png"), p_rank, width = 7, height = 14, dpi = 300)

## 6b. Immune vs Stromal score scatter, colored by Response
p_scatter <- ggplot(scores, aes(x = Stromal_Score, y = Immune_Score, color = Response)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(R = "#1b9e77", NR = "#d95f02")) +
  labs(title = "Immune vs stromal composite score - Gide cohort",
       x = "Stromal Score", y = "Immune Score") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "Immune_vs_Stromal_scatter_Gide.pdf"), p_scatter, width = 6, height = 5)
ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "Immune_vs_Stromal_scatter_Gide.png"), p_scatter, width = 6, height = 5, dpi = 300)

## 6c. Immune / Stromal score by Response (boxplot + Wilcoxon test)
box_df <- scores %>%
  select(Sample_id, Response, Immune_Score, Stromal_Score) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Immune_Score, Stromal_Score), names_to = "Score_type", values_to = "Score")

wilcox_immune <- wilcox.test(Immune_Score ~ Response, data = scores)
wilcox_stromal <- wilcox.test(Stromal_Score ~ Response, data = scores)

p_box <- ggplot(box_df, aes(x = Response, y = Score, fill = Response)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 1, alpha = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~Score_type) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(R = "#1b9e77", NR = "#d95f02")) +
  labs(title = "Immune / stromal scores by response to ICB - Gide cohort",
       subtitle = sprintf("Wilcoxon p (Immune) = %.3g | p (Stromal) = %.3g",
                           wilcox_immune$p.value, wilcox_stromal$p.value),
       y = "Composite z-score") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "Immune_Stromal_by_Response_Gide.pdf"), p_box, width = 7, height = 5)
ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "Immune_Stromal_by_Response_Gide.png"), p_box, width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300)

## 6d. Heatmap of all cell-type level z-scores, samples ordered by Immune Score
sample_order <- scores$Sample_id
heat_mat <- t(celltype_z[sample_order, , drop = FALSE])

col_annot <- data.frame(
  Response = gide_clin[sample_order, "Response"],
  Therapy = gide_clin[sample_order, "Therapy"],
  row.names = sample_order
)
row_annot <- data.frame(
  Category = celltype_category,
  row.names = colnames(celltype_z)
)

ann_colors <- list(
  Response = c(R = "#1b9e77", NR = "#d95f02"),
  Category = c(Immune = "#377eb8", Stromal = "#984ea3", Other = "#999999")
)

heat_mat[heat_mat > 3] <- 3
heat_mat[heat_mat < -3] <- -3

pheatmap(
  heat_mat,
  annotation_col = col_annot,
  annotation_row = row_annot,
  annotation_colors = ann_colors,
  cluster_cols = FALSE,
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  show_colnames = FALSE,
  color = colorRampPalette(rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")))(100),
  fontsize_row = 7,
  main = "Cell-type composite z-scores - Gide cohort (samples ranked by Immune Score)",
  filename = file.path(results_dir, "Heatmap_celltypes_Gide.pdf"),
  width = 12,
  height = 9
)
pheatmap(
  heat_mat,
  annotation_col = col_annot,
  annotation_row = row_annot,
  annotation_colors = ann_colors,
  cluster_cols = FALSE,
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  show_colnames = FALSE,
  color = colorRampPalette(rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")))(100),
  fontsize_row = 7,
  main = "Cell-type composite z-scores - Gide cohort (samples ranked by Immune Score)",
  filename = file.path(results_dir, "Heatmap_celltypes_Gide.png"),
  width = 12,
  height = 9,
  res = 300
)

## ---- 7. Run parameters log --------------------------------------------------

log_lines <- c(
  "Gide cohort TME characterization with multideconv",
  sprintf("Date: %s", Sys.Date()),
  sprintf("Samples: %d", nrow(scores)),
  "Input: data/Gide_log2TPM.txt, converted log2(TPM+1) -> linear TPM via 2^x - 1",
  "compute.deconvolution(methods = c('Quantiseq','Epidish','DeconRNASeq','DWLS'), normalized = FALSE, doParallel = TRUE, workers = 4)",
  "  (CBSX skipped: no CIBERSORTx credentials/Docker; MOMF skipped: no scRNA-seq reference available)",
  "compute.deconvolution.analysis(corr = 0.7, corr_type = 'spearman')",
  sprintf("Wilcoxon Immune Score R vs NR: p = %.4g", wilcox_immune$p.value),
  sprintf("Wilcoxon Stromal Score R vs NR: p = %.4g", wilcox_stromal$p.value),
  "Immune/Stromal/Other Score = mean of per-cell-type z-scores (cell types first averaged across their correlated subgroups, then averaged uniformly within category)"
)
writeLines(log_lines, file.path(results_dir, "analysis_log_Gide.txt"))

cat("Done. Results written to:", results_dir, "\n")

rownames(gide_clin) <- gide_clin$Sample_id

## Reverse log2(TPM + 1) back to linear TPM scale (multideconv expects raw counts or linear TPM)
tpm <- (2^as.matrix(log2tpm)) - 1
tpm[tpm < 0] <- 0

## ---- 2. Run deconvolution (first-generation methods, no scRNA-seq reference available) ----

old_wd <- getwd()
setwd(results_dir)

deconv <- compute.deconvolution(
  raw.counts = tpm,
  methods = c("Quantiseq", "Epidish", "DeconRNASeq", "DWLS"),
  normalized = FALSE,
  doParallel = TRUE,
  workers = 4,
  return = TRUE,
  file_name = "Gide"
)

## compute.deconvolution() builds its internal TPM data.frame with check.names = TRUE,
## which prepends "X" to sample IDs starting with a digit (all Gide IDs do). Restore
## the original sample IDs so they match the clinical table downstream.
name_map <- setNames(colnames(tpm), make.names(colnames(tpm)))
rownames(deconv) <- name_map[rownames(deconv)]

## ---- 3. Reduce redundancy / build per-cell-type subgroups ------------------

analysis <- compute.deconvolution.analysis(
  deconv,
  corr = 0.7,
  corr_type = "spearman",
  return = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  file_name = "Gide"
)

## Flatten the package's hardcoded Results/ subfolder into results/
if (dir.exists("Results")) {
  for (f in list.files("Results", full.names = TRUE)) {
    file.rename(f, file.path(results_dir, basename(f)))
  }
  unlink("Results", recursive = TRUE)
}

setwd(old_wd)

subgroup_mat <- analysis[["Deconvolution matrix"]]

## ---- 4. Classify cell types into Immune / Stromal / Other ------------------

immune_cells <- c(
  "B.cells", "B.naive.cells", "B.memory.cells", "Macrophages.cells", "Macrophages.M0",
  "Macrophages.M1", "Macrophages.M2", "Monocytes", "Neutrophils", "NK.cells",
  "NK.activated", "NK.resting", "NKT.cells", "CD4.cells", "CD4.memory.activated",
  "CD4.memory.resting", "CD4.naive", "CD8.cells", "CD4.regulatory", "CD4.non.regulatory",
  "T.cells.helper", "T.cells.gamma.delta", "Dendritic.cells", "Dendritic.activated.cells",
  "Dendritic.resting.cells", "Eosinophils", "Plasma", "Mast.cells", "Mast.activated.cells",
  "Mast.resting.cells", "Dendritic.plasmacytoid.cells", "Myeloid.cells", "Basophils",
  "T.cells.proliferative"
)
stromal_cells <- c("Endothelial", "Myocytes", "Fibroblasts", "CAF", "Pericytes", "Mural.cells")
other_cells <- c("Cancer", "Epithelial")

celltype_of_subgroup <- sub("_Subgroup\\.[0-9]+$", "", colnames(subgroup_mat))
category <- case_when(
  celltype_of_subgroup %in% immune_cells ~ "Immune",
  celltype_of_subgroup %in% stromal_cells ~ "Stromal",
  celltype_of_subgroup %in% other_cells ~ "Other",
  TRUE ~ "Unassigned"
)

feature_annot <- data.frame(
  Subgroup = colnames(subgroup_mat),
  Cell_type = celltype_of_subgroup,
  Category = category,
  row.names = colnames(subgroup_mat),
  check.names = FALSE
)
write.csv(feature_annot, file.path(results_dir, "Feature_cell_type_annotation_Gide.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## ---- 5. Composite Immune / Stromal scores per sample ------------------------
## Two-level z-scoring: subgroups of the same cell type are first averaged (so a
## cell type estimated by many correlated method-signature combinations does not
## dominate), then cell types are averaged uniformly within each category.

z_subgroups <- scale(as.matrix(subgroup_mat))

celltype_z <- sapply(split(colnames(subgroup_mat), celltype_of_subgroup), function(cols) {
  rowMeans(z_subgroups[, cols, drop = FALSE])
})
rownames(celltype_z) <- rownames(subgroup_mat)

celltype_category <- case_when(
  colnames(celltype_z) %in% immune_cells ~ "Immune",
  colnames(celltype_z) %in% stromal_cells ~ "Stromal",
  colnames(celltype_z) %in% other_cells ~ "Other",
  TRUE ~ "Unassigned"
)

scores <- data.frame(
  Sample_id = rownames(celltype_z),
  Immune_Score = rowMeans(celltype_z[, celltype_category == "Immune", drop = FALSE]),
  Stromal_Score = rowMeans(celltype_z[, celltype_category == "Stromal", drop = FALSE]),
  Other_Score = rowMeans(celltype_z[, celltype_category == "Other", drop = FALSE]),
  check.names = FALSE
)
scores$Immune_minus_Stromal <- scores$Immune_Score - scores$Stromal_Score

scores <- merge(scores, gide_clin[, c("Sample_id", "Response", "Therapy")], by = "Sample_id")
scores <- scores[, c("Sample_id", "Immune_Score", "Stromal_Score", "Other_Score", "Immune_minus_Stromal", "Response", "Therapy")]

scores <- scores[order(-scores$Immune_Score), ]
scores$Immune_Rank <- seq_len(nrow(scores))

write.csv(scores, file.path(results_dir, "Immune_Stromal_scores_Gide.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## ---- 6. Plots ---------------------------------------------------------------

## 6a. Ranked barplot of Immune Score per patient, colored by Response
plot_df <- scores
plot_df$Sample_id <- factor(plot_df$Sample_id, levels = plot_df$Sample_id[order(plot_df$Immune_Score)])

p_rank <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Sample_id, y = Immune_Score, fill = Response)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(R = "#1b9e77", NR = "#d95f02")) +
  labs(title = "Gide cohort - immune infiltration ranking", x = NULL,
       y = "Immune Score (mean z-score across immune cell types)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 8) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 5))

ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "Immune_score_ranking_Gide.pdf"), p_rank, width = 7, height = 14)
ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "Immune_score_ranking_Gide.png"), p_rank, width = 7, height = 14, dpi = 300)

## 6b. Immune vs Stromal score scatter, colored by Response
p_scatter <- ggplot(scores, aes(x = Stromal_Score, y = Immune_Score, color = Response)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(R = "#1b9e77", NR = "#d95f02")) +
  labs(title = "Immune vs stromal composite score - Gide cohort",
       x = "Stromal Score", y = "Immune Score") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "Immune_vs_Stromal_scatter_Gide.pdf"), p_scatter, width = 6, height = 5)
ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "Immune_vs_Stromal_scatter_Gide.png"), p_scatter, width = 6, height = 5, dpi = 300)

## 6c. Immune / Stromal score by Response (boxplot + Wilcoxon test)
box_df <- scores %>%
  select(Sample_id, Response, Immune_Score, Stromal_Score) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Immune_Score, Stromal_Score), names_to = "Score_type", values_to = "Score")

wilcox_immune <- wilcox.test(Immune_Score ~ Response, data = scores)
wilcox_stromal <- wilcox.test(Stromal_Score ~ Response, data = scores)

p_box <- ggplot(box_df, aes(x = Response, y = Score, fill = Response)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 1, alpha = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~Score_type) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(R = "#1b9e77", NR = "#d95f02")) +
  labs(title = "Immune / stromal scores by response to ICB - Gide cohort",
       subtitle = sprintf("Wilcoxon p (Immune) = %.3g | p (Stromal) = %.3g",
                           wilcox_immune$p.value, wilcox_stromal$p.value),
       y = "Composite z-score") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "Immune_Stromal_by_Response_Gide.pdf"), p_box, width = 7, height = 5)
ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "Immune_Stromal_by_Response_Gide.png"), p_box, width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300)

## 6d. Heatmap of all cell-type level z-scores, samples ordered by Immune Score
sample_order <- scores$Sample_id
heat_mat <- t(celltype_z[sample_order, , drop = FALSE])

col_annot <- data.frame(
  Response = gide_clin[sample_order, "Response"],
  Therapy = gide_clin[sample_order, "Therapy"],
  row.names = sample_order
)
row_annot <- data.frame(
  Category = celltype_category,
  row.names = colnames(celltype_z)
)

ann_colors <- list(
  Response = c(R = "#1b9e77", NR = "#d95f02"),
  Category = c(Immune = "#377eb8", Stromal = "#984ea3", Other = "#999999")
)

heat_mat[heat_mat > 3] <- 3
heat_mat[heat_mat < -3] <- -3

pheatmap(
  heat_mat,
  annotation_col = col_annot,
  annotation_row = row_annot,
  annotation_colors = ann_colors,
  cluster_cols = FALSE,
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  show_colnames = FALSE,
  color = colorRampPalette(rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")))(100),
  fontsize_row = 7,
  main = "Cell-type composite z-scores - Gide cohort (samples ranked by Immune Score)",
  filename = file.path(results_dir, "Heatmap_celltypes_Gide.pdf"),
  width = 12,
  height = 9
)
pheatmap(
  heat_mat,
  annotation_col = col_annot,
  annotation_row = row_annot,
  annotation_colors = ann_colors,
  cluster_cols = FALSE,
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  show_colnames = FALSE,
  color = colorRampPalette(rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")))(100),
  fontsize_row = 7,
  main = "Cell-type composite z-scores - Gide cohort (samples ranked by Immune Score)",
  filename = file.path(results_dir, "Heatmap_celltypes_Gide.png"),
  width = 12,
  height = 9,
  res = 300
)

## ---- 7. Run parameters log --------------------------------------------------

log_lines <- c(
  "Gide cohort TME characterization with multideconv",
  sprintf("Date: %s", Sys.Date()),
  sprintf("Samples: %d", nrow(scores)),
  "Input: data/Gide_log2TPM.txt, converted log2(TPM+1) -> linear TPM via 2^x - 1",
  "compute.deconvolution(methods = c('Quantiseq','Epidish','DeconRNASeq','DWLS'), normalized = FALSE, doParallel = TRUE, workers = 4)",
  "  (CBSX skipped: no CIBERSORTx credentials/Docker; MOMF skipped: no scRNA-seq reference available)",
  "compute.deconvolution.analysis(corr = 0.7, corr_type = 'spearman')",
  sprintf("Wilcoxon Immune Score R vs NR: p = %.4g", wilcox_immune$p.value),
  sprintf("Wilcoxon Stromal Score R vs NR: p = %.4g", wilcox_stromal$p.value),
  "Immune/Stromal/Other Score = mean of per-cell-type z-scores (cell types first averaged across their correlated subgroups, then averaged uniformly within category)"
)
writeLines(log_lines, file.path(results_dir, "analysis_log_Gide.txt"))

cat("Done. Results written to:", results_dir, "\n")

## Columns are either "<CellType>_Subgroup.<i>" (grouped features) or the raw
## "<method>_<signature>_<CellType>" (ungrouped singleton features, cell type
## names never contain "_" per multideconv's nomenclature).
extract_celltype <- function(x) {
  is_subgroup <- grepl("_Subgroup\\.[0-9]+$", x)
  out <- character(length(x))
  out[is_subgroup] <- sub("_Subgroup\\.[0-9]+$", "", x[is_subgroup])
  out[!is_subgroup] <- sub(".*_", "", x[!is_subgroup])
  out
}
celltype_of_subgroup <- extract_celltype(colnames(subgroup_mat))

#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
# TME (immune/stromal) characterization of the Gide melanoma ICB cohort using multideconv.

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(multideconv)
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(pheatmap)
  library(RColorBrewer)
})

set.seed(1)

work_dir <- "/home/marcelo.hurtado/Documents/tme_analysis/85d224db4e/work"
data_dir <- file.path(work_dir, "data")
results_dir <- file.path(work_dir, "results")

## ---- 1. Load data ----------------------------------------------------------

log2tpm <- read.delim(file.path(data_dir, "Gide_log2TPM.txt"), check.names = FALSE, row.names = 1)
coldata <- read.table(file.path(data_dir, "colData_all.txt"), header = TRUE, sep = " ", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

gide_clin <- coldata[coldata$Cohort == "Gide", ]
stopifnot(setequal(colnames(log2tpm), gide_clin$Sample_id))
gide_clin <- gide_clin[match(colnames(log2tpm), gide_clin$Sample_id), ]
rownames(gide_clin) <- gide_clin$Sample_id

## Reverse log2(TPM + 1) back to linear TPM scale (multideconv expects raw counts or linear TPM)
tpm <- (2^as.matrix(log2tpm)) - 1
tpm[tpm < 0] <- 0

## ---- 2. Run deconvolution (first-generation methods, no scRNA-seq reference available) ----

old_wd <- getwd()
setwd(results_dir)

deconv <- compute.deconvolution(
  raw.counts = tpm,
  methods = c("Quantiseq", "Epidish", "DeconRNASeq", "DWLS"),
  normalized = FALSE,
  doParallel = TRUE,
  workers = 4,
  return = TRUE,
  file_name = "Gide"
)

## compute.deconvolution() builds its internal TPM data.frame with check.names = TRUE,
## which prepends "X" to sample IDs starting with a digit (all Gide IDs do). Restore
## the original sample IDs so they match the clinical table downstream.
name_map <- setNames(colnames(tpm), make.names(colnames(tpm)))
rownames(deconv) <- name_map[rownames(deconv)]
write.csv(deconv, file.path(results_dir, "Deconvolution_Gide.csv"))

## ---- 3. Reduce redundancy / build per-cell-type subgroups ------------------

analysis <- compute.deconvolution.analysis(
  deconv,
  corr = 0.7,
  corr_type = "spearman",
  return = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  file_name = "Gide"
)

## Flatten the package's hardcoded Results/ subfolder into results/
if (dir.exists("Results")) {
  for (f in list.files("Results", full.names = TRUE)) {
    file.rename(f, file.path(results_dir, basename(f)))
  }
  unlink("Results", recursive = TRUE)
}

setwd(old_wd)

subgroup_mat <- analysis[["Deconvolution matrix"]]

## ---- 4. Classify cell types into Immune / Stromal / Other ------------------

immune_cells <- c(
  "B.cells", "B.naive.cells", "B.memory.cells", "Macrophages.cells", "Macrophages.M0",
  "Macrophages.M1", "Macrophages.M2", "Monocytes", "Neutrophils", "NK.cells",
  "NK.activated", "NK.resting", "NKT.cells", "CD4.cells", "CD4.memory.activated",
  "CD4.memory.resting", "CD4.naive", "CD8.cells", "CD4.regulatory", "CD4.non.regulatory",
  "T.cells.helper", "T.cells.gamma.delta", "Dendritic.cells", "Dendritic.activated.cells",
  "Dendritic.resting.cells", "Eosinophils", "Plasma", "Mast.cells", "Mast.activated.cells",
  "Mast.resting.cells", "Dendritic.plasmacytoid.cells", "Myeloid.cells", "Basophils",
  "T.cells.proliferative"
)
stromal_cells <- c("Endothelial", "Myocytes", "Fibroblasts", "CAF", "Pericytes", "Mural.cells")
other_cells <- c("Cancer", "Epithelial")

celltype_of_subgroup <- sub("_Subgroup\\.[0-9]+$", "", colnames(subgroup_mat))
category <- case_when(
  celltype_of_subgroup %in% immune_cells ~ "Immune",
  celltype_of_subgroup %in% stromal_cells ~ "Stromal",
  celltype_of_subgroup %in% other_cells ~ "Other",
  TRUE ~ "Unassigned"
)

feature_annot <- data.frame(
  Subgroup = colnames(subgroup_mat),
  Cell_type = celltype_of_subgroup,
  Category = category,
  row.names = colnames(subgroup_mat),
  check.names = FALSE
)
write.csv(feature_annot, file.path(results_dir, "Feature_cell_type_annotation_Gide.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## ---- 5. Composite Immune / Stromal scores per sample ------------------------
## Two-level z-scoring: subgroups of the same cell type are first averaged (so a
## cell type estimated by many correlated method-signature combinations does not
## dominate), then cell types are averaged uniformly within each category.

z_subgroups <- scale(as.matrix(subgroup_mat))

celltype_z <- sapply(split(colnames(subgroup_mat), celltype_of_subgroup), function(cols) {
  rowMeans(z_subgroups[, cols, drop = FALSE])
})
rownames(celltype_z) <- rownames(subgroup_mat)

celltype_category <- case_when(
  colnames(celltype_z) %in% immune_cells ~ "Immune",
  colnames(celltype_z) %in% stromal_cells ~ "Stromal",
  colnames(celltype_z) %in% other_cells ~ "Other",
  TRUE ~ "Unassigned"
)

scores <- data.frame(
  Sample_id = rownames(celltype_z),
  Immune_Score = rowMeans(celltype_z[, celltype_category == "Immune", drop = FALSE]),
  Stromal_Score = rowMeans(celltype_z[, celltype_category == "Stromal", drop = FALSE]),
  Other_Score = rowMeans(celltype_z[, celltype_category == "Other", drop = FALSE]),
  check.names = FALSE
)
scores$Immune_minus_Stromal <- scores$Immune_Score - scores$Stromal_Score

scores <- merge(scores, gide_clin[, c("Sample_id", "Response", "Therapy")], by = "Sample_id")
scores <- scores[, c("Sample_id", "Immune_Score", "Stromal_Score", "Other_Score", "Immune_minus_Stromal", "Response", "Therapy")]

scores <- scores[order(-scores$Immune_Score), ]
scores$Immune_Rank <- seq_len(nrow(scores))

write.csv(scores, file.path(results_dir, "Immune_Stromal_scores_Gide.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## ---- 6. Plots ---------------------------------------------------------------

## 6a. Ranked barplot of Immune Score per patient, colored by Response
plot_df <- scores
plot_df$Sample_id <- factor(plot_df$Sample_id, levels = plot_df$Sample_id[order(plot_df$Immune_Score)])

p_rank <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Sample_id, y = Immune_Score, fill = Response)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(R = "#1b9e77", NR = "#d95f02")) +
  labs(title = "Gide cohort - immune infiltration ranking", x = NULL,
       y = "Immune Score (mean z-score across immune cell types)") +

suppressPackageStartupMessages({

  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(pheatmap)
  library(RColorBrewer)
})

set.seed(1)

work_dir <- "/home/marcelo.hurtado/Documents/tme_analysis/85d224db4e/work"
data_dir <- file.path(work_dir, "data")
results_dir <- file.path(work_dir, "results")

## ---- 1. Load data ----------------------------------------------------------

log2tpm <- read.delim(file.path(data_dir, "Gide_log2TPM.txt"), check.names = FALSE, row.names = 1)
coldata <- read.table(file.path(data_dir, "colData_all.txt"), header = TRUE, sep = " ", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

gide_clin <- coldata[coldata$Cohort == "Gide", ]
stopifnot(setequal(colnames(log2tpm), gide_clin$Sample_id))
gide_clin <- gide_clin[match(colnames(log2tpm), gide_clin$Sample_id), ]
rownames(gide_clin) <- gide_clin$Sample_id

## Reverse log2(TPM + 1) back to linear TPM scale (multideconv expects raw counts or linear TPM)
tpm <- (2^as.matrix(log2tpm)) - 1
tpm[tpm < 0] <- 0

## ---- 2. Run deconvolution (first-generation methods, no scRNA-seq reference available) ----

old_wd <- getwd()
setwd(results_dir)

deconv <- compute.deconvolution(
  raw.counts = tpm,
  methods = c("Quantiseq", "Epidish", "DeconRNASeq", "DWLS"),
  normalized = FALSE,
  doParallel = TRUE,
  workers = 4,
  return = TRUE,
  file_name = "Gide"
)

## compute.deconvolution() builds its internal TPM data.frame with check.names = TRUE,
## which prepends "X" to sample IDs starting with a digit (all Gide IDs do). Restore
## the original sample IDs so they match the clinical table downstream.
name_map <- setNames(colnames(tpm), make.names(colnames(tpm)))
rownames(deconv) <- name_map[rownames(deconv)]
write.csv(deconv, file.path(results_dir, "Deconvolution_Gide.csv"))

## ---- 3. Reduce redundancy / build per-cell-type subgroups ------------------

analysis <- compute.deconvolution.analysis(
  deconv,
  corr = 0.7,
  corr_type = "spearman",
  return = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  file_name = "Gide"
)

## Flatten the package's hardcoded Results/ subfolder into results/
if (dir.exists("Results")) {

  "Macrophages.M1", "Macrophages.M2", "Monocytes", "Neutrophils", "NK.cells",
  "NK.activated", "NK.resting", "NKT.cells", "CD4.cells", "CD4.memory.activated",
  "CD4.memory.resting", "CD4.naive", "CD8.cells", "CD4.regulatory", "CD4.non.regulatory",
  "T.cells.helper", "T.cells.gamma.delta", "Dendritic.cells", "Dendritic.activated.cells",
  "Dendritic.resting.cells", "Eosinophils", "Plasma", "Mast.cells", "Mast.activated.cells",
  "Mast.resting.cells", "Dendritic.plasmacytoid.cells", "Myeloid.cells", "Basophils",
  "T.cells.proliferative"
)

other_cells <- c("Cancer", "Epithelial")

## "<method>_<signature>_<CellType>" (ungrouped singleton features, cell type
## names never contain "_" per multideconv's nomenclature).
extract_celltype <- function(x) {
  is_subgroup <- grepl("_Subgroup\\.[0-9]+$", x)
  out <- character(length(x))
  out[is_subgroup] <- sub("_Subgroup\\.[0-9]+$", "", x[is_subgroup])
  out[!is_subgroup] <- sub(".*_", "", x[!is_subgroup])
  out

  labs(title = "Gide cohort - immune infiltration ranking", x = NULL,
       y = "Immune Score (mean z-score across immune cell types)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 8) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 5))

ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "Immune_score_ranking_Gide.pdf"), p_rank, width = 7, height = 14)
ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "Immune_score_ranking_Gide.png"), p_rank, width = 7, height = 14, dpi = 300)

ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "Immune_vs_Stromal_scatter_Gide.png"), p_scatter, width = 6, height = 5, dpi = 300)

  out[!is_subgroup] <- sub(".*_", "", x[!is_subgroup])
  out
}
celltype_of_subgroup <- extract_celltype(colnames(subgroup_mat))
category <- case_when(
  celltype_of_subgroup %in% immune_cells ~ "Immune",
  celltype_of_subgroup %in% stromal_cells ~ "Stromal",
  celltype_of_subgroup %in% other_cells ~ "Other",
  TRUE ~ "Unassigned"
)

feature_annot <- data.frame(
  Subgroup = colnames(subgroup_mat),
  Cell_type = celltype_of_subgroup,
  Category = category,
  row.names = colnames(subgroup_mat),
  check.names = FALSE
)
write.csv(feature_annot, file.path(results_dir, "Feature_cell_type_annotation_Gide.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## ---- 5. Composite Immune / Stromal scores per sample ------------------------
## Two-level z-scoring: subgroups of the same cell type are first averaged (so a
## cell type estimated by many correlated method-signature combinations does not
## dominate), then cell types are averaged uniformly within each category.

z_subgroups <- scale(as.matrix(subgroup_mat))

celltype_z <- sapply(split(colnames(subgroup_mat), celltype_of_subgroup), function(cols) {
  rowMeans(z_subgroups[, cols, drop = FALSE])
})
rownames(celltype_z) <- rownames(subgroup_mat)

celltype_category <- case_when(
  colnames(celltype_z) %in% immune_cells ~ "Immune",
  colnames(celltype_z) %in% stromal_cells ~ "Stromal",
  colnames(celltype_z) %in% other_cells ~ "Other",
  TRUE ~ "Unassigned"
)

scores <- data.frame(
  Sample_id = rownames(celltype_z),
  Immune_Score = rowMeans(celltype_z[, celltype_category == "Immune", drop = FALSE]),
  Stromal_Score = rowMeans(celltype_z[, celltype_category == "Stromal", drop = FALSE]),
  Other_Score = rowMeans(celltype_z[, celltype_category == "Other", drop = FALSE]),
  check.names = FALSE
)
scores$Immune_minus_Stromal <- scores$Immune_Score - scores$Stromal_Score

scores <- merge(scores, gide_clin[, c("Sample_id", "Response", "Therapy")], by = "Sample_id")
scores <- scores[, c("Sample_id", "Immune_Score", "Stromal_Score", "Other_Score", "Immune_minus_Stromal", "Response", "Therapy")]

scores <- scores[order(-scores$Immune_Score), ]
scores$Immune_Rank <- seq_len(nrow(scores))

write.csv(scores, file.path(results_dir, "Immune_Stromal_scores_Gide.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## ---- 6. Plots ---------------------------------------------------------------

## 6a. Ranked barplot of Immune Score per patient, colored by Response
plot_df <- scores
plot_df$Sample_id <- factor(plot_df$Sample_id, levels = plot_df$Sample_id[order(plot_df$Immune_Score)])

p_rank <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Sample_id, y = Immune_Score, fill = Response)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(R = "#1b9e77", NR = "#d95f02")) +
  labs(title = "Gide cohort - immune infiltration ranking", x = NULL,
       y = "Immune Score (mean z-score across immune cell types)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 8) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 5))

ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "Immune_score_ranking_Gide.pdf"), p_rank, width = 7, height = 14)
ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "Immune_score_ranking_Gide.png"), p_rank, width = 7, height = 14, dpi = 300)

## 6b. Immune vs Stromal score scatter, colored by Response
p_scatter <- ggplot(scores, aes(x = Stromal_Score, y = Immune_Score, color = Response)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(R = "#1b9e77", NR = "#d95f02")) +
  labs(title = "Immune vs stromal composite score - Gide cohort",
       x = "Stromal Score", y = "Immune Score") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "Immune_vs_Stromal_scatter_Gide.pdf"), p_scatter, width = 6, height = 5)
ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "Immune_vs_Stromal_scatter_Gide.png"), p_scatter, width = 6, height = 5, dpi = 300)

## 6c. Immune / Stromal score by Response (boxplot + Wilcoxon test)
box_df <- scores %>%
  select(Sample_id, Response, Immune_Score, Stromal_Score) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Immune_Score, Stromal_Score), names_to = "Score_type", values_to = "Score")

wilcox_immune <- wilcox.test(Immune_Score ~ Response, data = scores)
wilcox_stromal <- wilcox.test(Stromal_Score ~ Response, data = scores)

p_box <- ggplot(box_df, aes(x = Response, y = Score, fill = Response)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 1, alpha = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~Score_type) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(R = "#1b9e77", NR = "#d95f02")) +
  labs(title = "Immune / stromal scores by response to ICB - Gide cohort",
       subtitle = sprintf("Wilcoxon p (Immune) = %.3g | p (Stromal) = %.3g",
                           wilcox_immune$p.value, wilcox_stromal$p.value),
       y = "Composite z-score") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "Immune_Stromal_by_Response_Gide.pdf"), p_box, width = 7, height = 5)
ggsave(file.path(results_dir, "Immune_Stromal_by_Response_Gide.png"), p_box, width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300)

## 6d. Heatmap of all cell-type level z-scores, samples ordered by Immune Score
sample_order <- scores$Sample_id
heat_mat <- t(celltype_z[sample_order, , drop = FALSE])

col_annot <- data.frame(
  Response = gide_clin[sample_order, "Response"],
  Therapy = gide_clin[sample_order, "Therapy"],
  row.names = sample_order
)
row_annot <- data.frame(
  Category = celltype_category,
  row.names = colnames(celltype_z)
)

ann_colors <- list(
  Response = c(R = "#1b9e77", NR = "#d95f02"),
  Category = c(Immune = "#377eb8", Stromal = "#984ea3", Other = "#999999")
)

heat_mat[heat_mat > 3] <- 3
heat_mat[heat_mat < -3] <- -3

pheatmap(
  heat_mat,
  annotation_col = col_annot,
  annotation_row = row_annot,
  annotation_colors = ann_colors,
  cluster_cols = FALSE,
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  show_colnames = FALSE,
  color = colorRampPalette(rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")))(100),
  fontsize_row = 7,
  main = "Cell-type composite z-scores - Gide cohort (samples ranked by Immune Score)",
  filename = file.path(results_dir, "Heatmap_celltypes_Gide.pdf"),
  width = 12,
  height = 9
)
pheatmap(
  heat_mat,
  annotation_col = col_annot,
  annotation_row = row_annot,
  annotation_colors = ann_colors,
  cluster_cols = FALSE,
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  show_colnames = FALSE,
  color = colorRampPalette(rev(brewer.pal(11, "RdBu")))(100),
  fontsize_row = 7,
  main = "Cell-type composite z-scores - Gide cohort (samples ranked by Immune Score)",
  filename = file.path(results_dir, "Heatmap_celltypes_Gide.png"),
  width = 12,
  height = 9,
  res = 300
)

## ---- 7. Run parameters log --------------------------------------------------

log_lines <- c(
  "Gide cohort TME characterization with multideconv",
  sprintf("Date: %s", Sys.Date()),
  sprintf("Samples: %d", nrow(scores)),
  "Input: data/Gide_log2TPM.txt, converted log2(TPM+1) -> linear TPM via 2^x - 1",
  "compute.deconvolution(methods = c('Quantiseq','Epidish','DeconRNASeq','DWLS'), normalized = FALSE, doParallel = TRUE, workers = 4)",
  "  (CBSX skipped: no CIBERSORTx credentials/Docker; MOMF skipped: no scRNA-seq reference available)",
  "compute.deconvolution.analysis(corr = 0.7, corr_type = 'spearman')",
  sprintf("Wilcoxon Immune Score R vs NR: p = %.4g", wilcox_immune$p.value),
  sprintf("Wilcoxon Stromal Score R vs NR: p = %.4g", wilcox_stromal$p.value),
  "Immune/Stromal/Other Score = mean of per-cell-type z-scores (cell types first averaged across their correlated subgroups, then averaged uniformly within category)"
)
writeLines(log_lines, file.path(results_dir, "analysis_log_Gide.txt"))

cat("Done. Results written to:", results_dir, "\n")

content.text:
The analysis is complete. Here's a summary:

## What was done

Using `multideconv` on the 73 Gide melanoma ICB samples (log2TPM reversed to linear TPM):
- Ran 4 first-generation deconvolution methods (Quantiseq, EpiDISH, DeconRNASeq, DWLS) across all bundled signatures (TIL10, LM22, 5× CBSX scRNA-seq references) — CBSX itself was skipped (no CIBERSORTx credentials/Docker) and MOMF was skipped (no scRNA-seq reference available)
- `compute.deconvolution.analysis()` collapsed the ~250 raw method-signature-celltype features into correlation-based subgroups per cell type (Spearman ≥ 0.7)
- Classified each of the 39 recovered cell types as **Immune** (31 types: T/B/NK/myeloid lineages) or **Stromal** (6 types: Fibroblasts, CAF, Endothelial, Pericytes, Mural, Myocytes), with Cancer/Epithelial kept as "Other"
- Built a composite **Immune Score** and **Stromal Score** per patient (two-level z-scoring: subgroups → cell type → category average, so no single cell type or method dominates)

## Key results (`results/`)
- `Immune_Stromal_scores_Gide.csv` — full ranked table, most → least immune-infiltrated. Top: `20_ipiPD1_PRE`, `27_PD1_PRE`, `6_PD1_PRE`; bottom: `17_ipiPD1_PRE`, `23_PD1_PRE`, `45_ipiPD1_PRE`
- `Immune_score_ranking_Gide.png/pdf` — all 73 patients ranked, colored by response
- `Heatmap_celltypes_Gide.png/pdf` — full cell-type composition heatmap
- `Immune_vs_Stromal_scatter_Gide.png/pdf` and `Immune_Stromal_by_Response_Gide.png/pdf` — composition vs. ICB response (R/NR)
- `Deconvolution_Gide.csv`, `Deconvolution_after_subgrouping_Gide.csv`, `Cell_subgroups_Gide.csv`, `Feature_cell_type_annotation_Gide.csv` — full intermediate deconvolution outputs
- `analysis_log_Gide.txt` — run parameters for reproducibility

Note: immune/stromal scores did not differ significantly by response in this cohort (Wilcoxon p = 0.38 immune, p = 0.08 stromal) — a trend toward lower stromal content in responders, but not significant at this sample size.

Two bugs in the wrapper script were caught and fixed along the way (sample-ID mangling from `data.frame()`'s `check.names`, and ungrouped features keeping raw column names) — both documented in a memory note for future runs.

The analysis is finished. Do not run anything else. Answer these questions about what you did, briefly and factually:
1. Input data: did you transform the expression values before using them (for example from log2 to linear TPM)? For which steps, and why?
2. Methods: which methods or functions did you run? Which available methods or steps did you skip, and why?
3. Parameters: which parameters did you set to a value other than the default, and why?
4. Problems: which errors or unexpected results did you meet, and how did you handle each one?
5. Checks: what did you verify before trusting the results?
6. Limits: what is incomplete, uncertain or should be interpreted with caution?

content.text:
**1. Input data transformation**
Yes. `Gide_log2TPM.txt` is log2(TPM+1). I reversed it to linear TPM via `2^x - 1` (floored at 0) before deconvolution, because `multideconv`'s methods expect raw counts or linear TPM, not log-transformed values. This was done once, upstream of all deconvolution methods.

**2. Methods run / skipped**
Ran `compute.deconvolution()` with methods `Quantiseq`, `Epidish`, `DeconRNASeq`, `DWLS`, across all bundled signatures (TIL10, LM22, 5× CBSX scRNA-seq refs), then `compute.deconvolution.analysis()` for correlation-based subgrouping.
Skipped: `CBSX` (needs CIBERSORTx credentials + Docker, neither available), `MOMF` and all second-generation methods (`Autogenes`, `BayesPrism`, `Bisque`, `CPM`, `MuSic`, `SCDC`) — these require a single-cell reference matrix, which was not provided or requested.

**3. Non-default parameters**
- `normalized = FALSE` (default `TRUE`) — because the input was already TPM-normalized (after my log-reversal), not raw counts.
- `doParallel = TRUE`, `workers = 4` (default `FALSE`/`NULL`) — to speed up DWLS, chosen conservatively given the machine's limited free RAM rather than using all cores.
- `corr = 0.7`, `corr_type = "spearman"` in `compute.deconvolution.analysis()` — these are actually the function defaults, not changed.
- `zero_thr`, `cv_thr`, `batch` left at defaults.

**4. Problems encountered and handling**
- First run: `compute.deconvolution()` internally builds a `data.frame()` with `check.names = TRUE` on the TPM matrix, which prepended `"X"` to all sample IDs (they start with digits, e.g. `10_PD1_PRE` → `X10_PD1_PRE`). This broke the later merge with clinical data (produced an empty/near-empty scores table, which only surfaced downstream as a Wilcoxon-test error). Fixed by rebuilding a name map (`make.names(colnames(tpm))` → original) and restoring original sample IDs on `deconv` right after the call.
- Second run: my cell-type-extraction regex assumed all output columns followed `<CellType>_Subgroup.<i>`, but ungrouped (singleton) features keep their raw `method_signature_celltype` name instead. This misclassified many columns as "Unassigned" cell types. Fixed by adding a second parsing branch: strip the `_Subgroup.N` suffix when present, otherwise take the last `_`-delimited token as the cell type.
- Minor: `pheatmap` errored because an annotation factor level ("Unassigned") had no matching color; fixed by adding a fallback color and also classifying `uncharacterized_cell` under "Other".
- Each fix required a full rerun of the pipeline (~8–9 min each), since no intermediate objects were cached outside the package's own per-method cache (which is deleted on success).

**5. Checks performed before trusting results**
- Verified all 73 Gide sample IDs in the expression matrix exactly matched `Sample_id` in the clinical table (no missing/extra samples) and no duplicate gene symbols in the expression file.
- Confirmed required R packages/optional dependencies (`DeconRNASeq`, `DWLS`, `immunedeconv`, `EpiDISH`, `ADImpute`, `omnideconv`) were installed before running.
- After the fixes, re-checked that `Immune_Stromal_scores_Gide.csv` had 73 non-empty rows with sensible value ranges, and visually inspected the heatmap and boxplot outputs to confirm category annotations and color legends rendered correctly (no "Unassigned" cells left dangling in categories, Response/Therapy annotations aligned).
- Monitored memory/CPU during the DWLS parallel step (RAM dropped to ~250MB free with some swap use but did not OOM or crash).

**6. Limits / caveats**
- Immune/Stromal/Other scores are a composite z-score heuristic I defined (two-level averaging: subgroup → cell type → category), not a built-in `multideconv` function — it's a reasonable but not uniquely-validated way to combine heterogeneous proportion scales across methods.
- CIBERSORTx and all single-cell-based (second-generation) methods were entirely excluded, so the cell-type estimates rest only on first-generation, signature-based methods.
- The log2→TPM reversal assumes the data was generated as `log2(TPM+1)`; I did not have independent confirmation of this from the data source, only a plausibility check (TPM=0 cases land exactly at log2 value 0 under this assumption, which matched the observed column of zeros).
- Immune/Stromal score differences by response (R vs NR) were not statistically significant (Wilcoxon p = 0.38 and 0.08) — likely underpowered at n=73 with imbalanced groups (46 R / 27 NR); this should be read as descriptive, not a validated biomarker association.
- "Epithelial" and "Cancer" were placed in an "Other" bucket excluded from both Immune and Stromal scores; depending on the biological question, one or both could reasonably be folded into "Stromal"/parenchymal framing instead.

This broke the later merge with clinical data (produced an empty/near-empty scores table, which only surfaced downstream as a Wilcoxon-test error). Fixed by rebuilding a name map (`make.names(colnames(tpm))` → original) and restoring original sample IDs on `deconv` right after the call.
- Second run: my cell-type-extraction regex assumed all output columns followed `<CellType>_Subgroup.<i>`, but ungrouped (singleton) features keep their raw `method_signature_celltype` name instead. This misclassified many columns as "Unassigned" cell types. Fixed by adding a second parsing branch: strip the `_Subgroup.N` suffix when present, otherwise take the last `_`-delimited token as the cell type.
- Minor: `pheatmap` errored because an annotation factor level ("Unassigned") had no matching color; fixed by adding a fallback color and also classifying `uncharacterized_cell` under "Other".
- Each fix required a full rerun of the pipeline (~8–9 min each), since no intermediate objects were cached outside the package's own per-method cache (which is deleted on success).

**5. Checks performed before trusting results**
- Verified all 73 Gide sample IDs in the expression matrix exactly matched `Sample_id` in the clinical table (no missing/extra samples) and no duplicate gene symbols in the expression file.
- Confirmed required R packages/optional dependencies (`DeconRNASeq`, `DWLS`, `immunedeconv`, `EpiDISH`, `ADImpute`, `omnideconv`) were installed before running.
- After the fixes, re-checked that `Immune_Stromal_scores_Gide.csv` had 73 non-empty rows with sensible value ranges, and visually inspected the heatmap and boxplot outputs to confirm category annotations and color legends rendered correctly (no "Unassigned" cells left dangling in categories, Response/Therapy annotations aligned).
- Monitored memory/CPU during the DWLS parallel step (RAM dropped to ~250MB free with some swap use but did not OOM or crash).

**6. Limits / caveats**
- Immune/Stromal/Other scores are a composite z-score heuristic I defined (two-level averaging: subgroup → cell type → category), not a built-in `multideconv` function — it's a reasonable but not uniquely-validated way to combine heterogeneous proportion scales across methods.
- CIBERSORTx and all single-cell-based (second-generation) methods were entirely excluded, so the cell-type estimates rest only on first-generation, signature-based methods.
- The log2→TPM reversal assumes the data was generated as `log2(TPM+1)`; I did not have independent confirmation of this from the data source, only a plausibility check (TPM=0 cases land exactly at log2 value 0 under this assumption, which matched the observed column of zeros).
- Immune/Stromal score differences by response (R vs NR) were not statistically significant (Wilcoxon p = 0.38 and 0.08) — likely underpowered at n=73 with imbalanced groups (46 R / 27 NR); this should be read as descriptive, not a validated biomarker association.
- "Epithelial" and "Cancer" were placed in an "Other" bucket excluded from both Immune and Stromal scores; depending on the biological question, one or both could reasonably be folded into "Stromal"/parenchymal framing instead.
